A.explanation: This is $\frac{Q}{W}$ with units $\text{C J}^{-1}$, which is the inverse of a volt.

B.explanation: Charge per unit time is $\frac{Q}{t}$ with units $\text{C s}^{-1}$, which is current in amperes.

C.explanation: Energy transferred per unit charge is $\frac{W}{Q}$ with units $\text{J C}^{-1}$, which is the volt, the unit of e.m.f.

D.explanation: Energy transferred per unit time is $\frac{W}{t}$ with units $\text{J s}^{-1}$, which is power in watts.

Check units: $W$ is in joules $\text{J}$ and $Q$ is in coulombs $\text{C}$, so e.m.f. has units $\text{J C}^{-1}$.
Compare the options: only energy transferred per unit charge has the form $\text{J C}^{-1}$, while the others give $\text{C J}^{-1}$, $\text{C s}^{-1}$ and $\text{J s}^{-1}$.
